title: The Clinic Growth Show: Dr. Neha Sharma on missed calls, no-shows and honest pricing

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Welcome back to The Clinic Growth Show. Today I'm with Dr. Neha Sharma, who runs SmileCraft Dental in Pune. Neha, thanks for coming on.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: Thanks for having me. I've listened to this show for two years, so this is a bit surreal.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Let's start at the beginning. How did SmileCraft start?

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: I opened with one chair and one assistant in 2016. I had savings for exactly six months of rent, so the first year was pure survival.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: What was the hardest part of that first year?

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: Not the dentistry. The dentistry I knew. The hard part was that the phone kept ringing while my hands were inside someone's mouth.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: We counted once. In one month we missed 140 calls. If even a third of those were new patients, that's more than forty people who called a competitor instead.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: That's a big number. What did you do about it?

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: At first, nothing clever. I asked my assistant to call everyone back at lunch. But by lunch, most of them had already booked somewhere else.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: A missed call is not a missed call. It's a patient who chose someone else because we didn't pick up.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: So speed matters more than we think.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: Speed is everything. People call three clinics and book with whoever answers first. Nobody compares your degrees at that moment.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Let's talk about no-shows. Every clinic owner I talk to complains about them.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: We had a no-show rate of almost 22 percent in 2019. That's one in five chairs empty for an hour, every single day.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: We started sending a WhatsApp reminder the evening before, with a simple question: reply 1 to confirm, 2 to reschedule. Within three months no-shows dropped to 8 percent.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Why do you think that worked so well?

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: Because rescheduling became easy. Most no-shows aren't rude people. They're people who felt awkward calling to cancel.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: If you make cancelling easy, people cancel instead of disappearing. And a cancellation you know about is a slot you can fill.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: That's a nice way to put it. What about pricing? Dentistry has a reputation for surprise bills.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: Every patient at SmileCraft gets a written treatment plan with prices before we start. No exceptions, even for a simple filling.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: When we started doing that, our treatment acceptance went up, not down. People say yes when they aren't afraid of the bill.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Interesting. Most people assume showing prices scares patients away.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: Uncertainty scares patients away. A clear number, even a big one, lets them plan.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Let's talk about children. Kids' dentistry is its own world.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: With children, the first visit is not about teeth. It's about trust. We don't do any treatment on the first visit unless it's an emergency.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: We let them sit in the chair, press the buttons, look at the mirror. A child who leaves smiling comes back without a fight.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: And the parents?

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: Parents are watching how you treat their child more than how you treat the tooth. That's your real marketing.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: How do you think about reviews? Google reviews seem to decide everything now.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: We have about 380 Google reviews and I've read every one of them. The bad ones taught me more than the good ones.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: Almost every bad review was about waiting, not about the treatment. So we fixed the waiting.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: How?

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: We stopped double-booking to cover no-shows, because the reminders fixed the no-shows. And we text patients if we're running more than fifteen minutes late.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: A patient who knows you're running late is patient. A patient who doesn't know is angry. Same delay, different review.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Let's talk about your team. How many people now?

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: Eleven people and four chairs. The front desk is the hardest role to hire for, by far.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: Your front desk person is the first and last face of your clinic. I'd rather hire for warmth and train the software than the other way round.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: What does a great front desk person do differently?

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: They remember names. They notice when someone is nervous. And they never say 'we're fully booked' without offering the next slot.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: You mentioned software. How much technology do you use?

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: We were one of the first clinics in Kothrud to use an intraoral scanner. Patients see their own teeth on a screen, and suddenly they understand why they need the treatment.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: Showing beats telling. When a patient sees the crack on the screen, I don't have to convince anyone.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: What about AI? Everyone's talking about it.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: We use an AI assistant now for calls after hours and for WhatsApp questions. It answers the boring questions, like timings and parking, and books appointments into our calendar.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: Last month it booked 31 appointments outside clinic hours. Those are people who would have called someone else in the morning.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Were you worried patients would hate talking to a bot?

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: I was. But it tells them it's an assistant, and it hands over to my team the moment someone is in pain or upset. People don't mind a bot. They mind being ignored.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Let's talk about marketing. What has worked for you?

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: Honestly, community dental camps. We do one school camp every month, free check-ups. It's the best marketing we've ever done.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: We've screened over 3,000 children in those camps. Many of their parents are our patients now.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: Paid ads brought us clicks. Camps brought us families. Families stay for twenty years.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: What about Sunday openings? I hear you're open on Sundays.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: We open on Sunday mornings. It's now our busiest half-day of the week, because that's when working parents can actually come.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Doesn't that burn out your team?

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: We rotate. Nobody works more than two Sundays a month, and Sunday shifts get a day off in the week. Burned-out staff give burned-out care.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Let's talk about mistakes. What would you do differently if you started today?

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: I would track numbers from day one. For three years I ran the clinic on feelings. I thought we were busy. We were busy, but not profitable.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: The day I looked at revenue per chair hour, everything changed. Some treatments I loved were actually losing us money.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: That's brave to admit.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: Every clinic owner I know has a treatment they're proud of that quietly loses money. Measure it before you promote it.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: One last question. What advice would you give a dentist opening their first clinic next year?

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: Answer every call, keep your promises on price, and be kind to nervous patients. Everything else, you can learn on the way.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Dr. Neha Sharma, thank you so much.

segments.speaker: Dr. Neha Sharma
segments.text: Thank you. This was fun.
